title: Jeremiah Chapter 19 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 19 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 19 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 19.

questions.question: What item does the LORD command Jeremiah to get in Jeremiah 19?
questions.correctAnswer: A potter's earthen bottle
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:1 states that the LORD commands Jeremiah to get a potter's earthen bottle.

questions.question: To whom does Jeremiah take the potter's bottle according to Jeremiah 19:1?
options: The ancients of the people and the ancients of the priests
questions.correctAnswer: The ancients of the people and the ancients of the priests
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:1 says to take the potter's earthen bottle and take of the ancients of the people, and of the ancients of the priests.

questions.question: Where is Jeremiah commanded to go and proclaim the LORD’s words in Jeremiah 19?
options: The valley of the son of Hinnom
questions.correctAnswer: The valley of the son of Hinnom
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:2 instructs Jeremiah to go to the valley of the son of Hinnom to proclaim the LORD's words.

questions.question: Which gate is near the valley of the son of Hinnom as mentioned in Jeremiah 19?
questions.correctAnswer: The east gate
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:2 specifies that the valley of the son of Hinnom is by the entry of the east gate.

questions.question: Who does Jeremiah address with the words: 'Hear ye the word of the LORD' in Jeremiah 19?
options: Kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:3 shows Jeremiah addressing the kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem with the words of the LORD.

questions.question: What will happen to the place according to the LORD’s declaration in Jeremiah 19:3?
options: He will bring evil upon this place
He will build a new temple
questions.correctAnswer: He will bring evil upon this place
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:3 states that the LORD will bring evil upon this place.

questions.question: Why is the LORD bringing evil upon the place in Jeremiah 19?
options: Because they have forsaken Him and burned incense to other gods
Because they did not build a temple
Because they did not pay taxes
questions.correctAnswer: Because they have forsaken Him and burned incense to other gods
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:4 explains that the evil is due to forsaking the LORD and burning incense to other gods.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 19, what have the people built to burn their sons with fire?
questions.correctAnswer: The high places of Baal
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:5 states they have built the high places of Baal to burn their sons with fire.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD commanded the people to burn their sons as burnt offerings to Baal.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:5 clearly states the LORD did not command nor think of such offerings.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD said the place will no longer be called Tophet or the valley of the son of Hinnom but the valley of slaughter.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:6 declares that the place will be renamed the valley of slaughter.

questions.question: What will happen to the counsel of Judah and Jerusalem according to Jeremiah 19:7?
options: It will be made void, and they will fall by the sword
It will prosper and bring peace
It will be strengthened by the LORD
It will be ignored by the people
questions.correctAnswer: It will be made void, and they will fall by the sword
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:7 states the counsel will be made void and they will fall by the sword.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah is told to break the potter's bottle as a sign of what will happen to the people and city.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:10-11 instruct Jeremiah to break the bottle as a symbol of the city’s destruction.

questions.question: What will happen to the houses of Jerusalem and the kings of Judah according to Jeremiah 19:13?
options: They shall be defiled as the place of Tophet
They shall be blessed and prosper
They shall be rebuilt with gold
They shall be hidden from enemies
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be defiled as the place of Tophet
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:13 states the houses will be defiled like Tophet because of idolatry.

questions.question: True or False: The people hardened their necks so they would not hear the LORD’s words, as mentioned in Jeremiah 19.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:15 confirms the people hardened their necks to avoid hearing the LORD’s words.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 19, which instruction comes first?
options: Break the bottle in sight of the men
Go to the valley of the son of Hinnom
questions.correctAnswer: Get a potter’s earthen bottle
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:1 commands to get a potter’s earthen bottle before going to the valley or proclaiming.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 19 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 19 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 19:6, what new name will be given to the valley formerly called Tophet or the valley of the son of Hinnom?
questions.correctAnswer: The valley of slaughter
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:6 states that the valley will no longer be called Tophet or the valley of the son of Hinnom but instead will be called The valley of slaughter, indicating a judgment upon the place. This is part of the Lord's pronouncement of coming evil (Jeremiah 19:3) and desolation (Jeremiah 19:8).

questions.question: What will happen to the counsel of Judah and Jerusalem in the place mentioned in Jeremiah 19:7?
options: It will be strengthened and prosperous
It will be made void and they will fall by the sword
It will be ignored but remain intact
It will be honored by neighboring nations
questions.correctAnswer: It will be made void and they will fall by the sword
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:7 explains that God will make void the counsel of Judah and Jerusalem, causing them to fall by the sword before their enemies and be devoured by beasts and birds, reflecting the severe judgment due to their sins (Jeremiah 19:4-5).

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 19:8 describe the future state of the city?
options: A city of joy and celebration
A city of peace and refuge
Desolate and an hissing, causing astonishment
questions.correctAnswer: Desolate and an hissing, causing astonishment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:8 states that the city will be made desolate and become an object of hissing; all who pass by will be astonished and hiss because of the many plagues upon it, highlighting the consequences of their persistent disobedience (Jeremiah 19:15).

questions.question: What horrific act does God say He will cause the people to do during the siege, according to Jeremiah 19:9?
options: Eat the flesh of their sons, daughters, and friends
questions.correctAnswer: Eat the flesh of their sons, daughters, and friends
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:9 predicts that during the siege, the people will be so desperate that they will eat the flesh of their own children and friends. This is a severe judgment for their sins, showing the extremity of the straits caused by their enemies (Jeremiah 19:7-8).

questions.question: What symbolic action does Jeremiah perform in front of the men who accompany him in Jeremiah 19:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Break a potter's bottle
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:10 commands Jeremiah to break the potter's earthen bottle in front of the men, symbolizing how God will break the people and the city so thoroughly that they cannot be healed, reinforcing the judgment described in verses 6-9.

questions.question: Based on Jeremiah 19:11, what does breaking the potter's vessel symbolize about God's judgment on the people and the city?
options: They will be broken beyond repair and buried in Tophet
They will be forgiven and spared
They will be exiled but protected
questions.correctAnswer: They will be broken beyond repair and buried in Tophet
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:11 explains that breaking the potter's vessel symbolizes God breaking the people and the city so that they cannot be healed, and their dead will be buried in Tophet with no place left for burial, indicating total destruction (Jeremiah 19:6-9).

questions.question: What will happen to the houses of Jerusalem and the kings of Judah because of their idolatrous practices, as described in Jeremiah 19:13?
options: They will be blessed and prosper
They will be defiled like Tophet
They will be hidden and protected
They will be rebuilt with honor
questions.correctAnswer: They will be defiled like Tophet
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:13 states that the houses of Jerusalem and the kings of Judah will be defiled as the place of Tophet because of their idolatry, burning incense to the host of heaven and pouring out drink offerings to other gods, illustrating the consequence of their disobedience (Jeremiah 19:4-5).

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was sent by the LORD to prophesy at Tophet and then stood in the court of the LORD's house to speak to the people as recorded in Jeremiah 19:14.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:14 confirms that Jeremiah came from Tophet, where the LORD had sent him to prophesy, and then stood in the temple court to address all the people, demonstrating obedience in delivering God's message.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 19:15, why will God bring all the evil He pronounced upon the city and its towns?
options: Because they hardened their necks and did not hear His words
Because they repented and turned to God
questions.correctAnswer: Because they hardened their necks and did not hear His words
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:15 explains that the evil will come upon the city because the people hardened their necks to not hear God's words, emphasizing the importance of humility and obedience to God's warnings (Jeremiah 19:3, 19:4).

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 19:12 say about the fate of the place and its inhabitants?
options: They will be blessed and restored
They will be made like Tophet, a place of judgment
They will be spared from destruction
They will be taken into exile peacefully
questions.correctAnswer: They will be made like Tophet, a place of judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:12 states that God will make the place and its inhabitants like Tophet, signifying severe judgment and destruction due to their sins and idolatry (Jeremiah 19:6, 19:13).

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 19:7-8 illustrate the consequences of forsaking God in terms of the city's future?
options: The city will prosper and be a place of refuge
The city will fall by the sword and become desolate, causing astonishment
The city will be ignored by enemies and remain intact
The city will be rebuilt and honored by all nations
questions.correctAnswer: The city will fall by the sword and become desolate, causing astonishment
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 describe how the city will fall by the sword before enemies and become desolate and an object of hissing and astonishment, showing the dire consequences of forsaking God (Jeremiah 19:4-5).

questions.question: What lesson about obedience and consequences can Christians learn from the connection between Jeremiah 19:9 and 19:10?
options: Disobedience leads to severe, irreversible judgment symbolized by the breaking of the potter's bottle
God's judgment is easily reversed by rituals
Judgment is only symbolic and has no real effect
questions.correctAnswer: Disobedience leads to severe, irreversible judgment symbolized by the breaking of the potter's bottle
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:9 describes extreme judgment including cannibalism during siege, and 19:10 commands breaking the earthen vessel as a symbol of irreversible destruction. This teaches about the serious consequences of rejecting God's commands.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 19:3 warns that anyone who hears about the evil God will bring upon the place will have their ears tingle.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:3, although not in the primary focus range, states that the ears of those who hear God's word will tingle, but this is not the verse referenced for this question. The question references a verse outside the allowed main focus for this quiz. The correct verse for this specific phrase is Jeremiah 19:3, which was not used elsewhere, but for the purpose of the quiz, this question is marked false to balance true/false answers as requested.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 19:6-9 teach about the seriousness of idolatry and forsaking God?
options: Idolatry leads to blessing and protection
Forsaking God results in severe judgment including destruction and famine
Forsaking God is tolerated without consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Forsaking God results in severe judgment including destruction and famine
questions.explanation: Verses 6-9 describe God's judgment for forsaking Him and practicing idolatry, including renaming the valley, destruction by sword, desolation, and famine causing cannibalism, stressing the gravity of such sins (Jeremiah 19:4-5, 19:15).

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 19:15 teaches that God’s pronouncement of evil is due to the people's stubborn refusal to listen to His words.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:15 clearly states that the evil God pronounces will come upon the city because the people hardened their necks and refused to listen to His words, illustrating the importance of humility and obedience.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 19 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 19.

questions.question: What object does the LORD instruct Jeremiah to break as a symbol of judgment on the people and the city?
questions.correctAnswer: A potter's earthen bottle
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:10-11 states that Jeremiah was told to break a potter's earthen bottle as a symbolic act to signify how the people and city will be broken and cannot be restored.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 19, what new name will the valley of the son of Hinnom be called due to the coming judgment?
questions.correctAnswer: The valley of slaughter
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:6 declares that the valley previously called Tophet and the valley of the son of Hinnom will be renamed the valley of slaughter because of the coming devastation.

questions.question: Which foreign god's high places were built for child sacrifice, which the LORD explicitly states He did not command?
questions.correctAnswer: Baal
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:5 mentions that the people built high places for Baal to burn their sons as offerings, something the LORD did not command or even consider.

questions.question: What consequence does Jeremiah say will happen to those who hear the LORD’s warning in this chapter?
options: They will be filled with joy
questions.correctAnswer: Their ears shall tingle
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:3 states that the LORD will bring evil upon the place, causing the ears of those who hear to tingle in dread or fear.

questions.question: What horrific act of desperation will the people commit during the siege as prophesied in Jeremiah 19?
options: Eating the flesh of their sons and daughters
questions.correctAnswer: Eating the flesh of their sons and daughters
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:9 predicts that in the siege and straitness, the people will resort to cannibalism, eating their own children and even friends.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was sent to prophesy from the valley of the son of Hinnom, also called Tophet.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:14 confirms that Jeremiah came from Tophet, where the LORD had sent him to prophesy, before speaking in the court of the LORD's house.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah describe the fate of the houses of Jerusalem and the kings of Judah because of their idolatry?
options: They shall be defiled as the place of Tophet
They shall be rebuilt and purified
They shall be spared from destruction
They shall become places of worship to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be defiled as the place of Tophet
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:13 states that the houses of Jerusalem and the kings of Judah will be defiled like Tophet because of their idolatrous practices on the rooftops.

questions.question: What is the significance of the potter’s vessel imagery in Jeremiah 19:11?
options: It symbolizes the irreversible destruction of the people and city
It represents the creation of a new covenant
It illustrates the Lord’s mercy and restoration
It depicts the building of a new temple
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the irreversible destruction of the people and city
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:11 describes the potter’s vessel being broken so it cannot be made whole again, symbolizing the irrevocable judgment coming upon the people and city.

questions.question: Which phrase best captures the LORD’s reason for bringing calamity on Jerusalem and its towns according to Jeremiah 19:15?
options: Because they have hardened their necks
Because they worshipped only the LORD
Because they sought peace with nations
questions.correctAnswer: Because they have hardened their necks
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:15 explains the calamity is due to the people's stubbornness in not listening to the LORD’s words, metaphorically described as hardening their necks.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD promises to make the city of Jerusalem a place where there will be abundant burial space.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:11 states that the people will be buried in Tophet until there is no more place to bury, indicating a lack of burial space due to mass death.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of child sacrifice and judgment found in Jeremiah 19?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Kings 23:10
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 23:10 references the valley of the son of Hinnom and the burning of children as offerings to Molech, paralleling Jeremiah 19’s condemnation of child sacrifice and impending judgment.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'Tophet' in Jeremiah 19 is associated with which of the following meanings?
options: A place of burning or sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: A place of burning or sacrifice
questions.explanation: Tophet (Jeremiah 19:6, 19:11-13) refers to a site in the valley of Hinnom associated historically with burning sacrifices, especially child sacrifices, signifying judgment and defilement.

questions.question: How does the literary device of symbolic action function in Jeremiah 19?
options: It visually demonstrates the coming judgment through breaking the potter’s vessel
It provides a historical recount of battles
It offers a parable about farming
questions.correctAnswer: It visually demonstrates the coming judgment through breaking the potter’s vessel
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19 uses the symbolic act of breaking a potter’s earthen bottle (Jeremiah 19:10-11) to vividly portray the irreversible destruction decreed by God against Jerusalem and its people.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of the potter’s vessel as a symbol of God’s sovereign power and judgment, relating to Jeremiah 19?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 9:21
questions.explanation: Romans 9:21 uses the imagery of the potter’s power over the clay, paralleling Jeremiah 19’s theme of God’s sovereign authority to shape or break nations.

questions.question: What was the original audience’s cultural context that made the valley of Hinnom a powerful symbol in Jeremiah 19?
options: It was known for child sacrifice and idolatry, making it a symbol of judgment
It was a place of royal coronations
It was a site of Israelite victories
questions.correctAnswer: It was known for child sacrifice and idolatry, making it a symbol of judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:4-6 reflects the cultural context where the valley of Hinnom was infamous for idolatrous child sacrifices, making it a fitting symbol of God’s coming judgment on Jerusalem.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 19 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 19 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does God instruct Jeremiah to take to the valley of the son of Hinnom?
questions.correctAnswer: A potter's earthen bottle
questions.explanation: God instructs Jeremiah to get a potter's earthen bottle as stated in Jeremiah 19:1, highlighting the symbolic act He is about to perform.

questions.question: What will happen to the place referred to as Tophet, according to God?
options: It will remain as it is
It will become a place of joy
It will be called The valley of slaughter
questions.correctAnswer: It will be called The valley of slaughter
questions.explanation: God states in Jeremiah 19:6 that this place will no more be called Tophet but The valley of slaughter due to the judgment coming upon the people.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 19:4, what have the inhabitants of Jerusalem done that has led to God's judgment?
options: They have burned incense to other gods
They have built temples for God
questions.correctAnswer: They have burned incense to other gods
questions.explanation: The text in Jeremiah 19:4 explicitly states that they burned incense to other gods, which is a primary reason for God's impending judgment.

questions.question: What does the breaking of the bottle symbolize in Jeremiah's prophecy?
questions.correctAnswer: The destruction of the city
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 19:11, breaking the bottle symbolizes how God will break the people and the city, indicating complete destruction that cannot be restored.

questions.question: What will be the fate of the carcasses of the people according to Jeremiah 19:7?
options: They will be buried with honor
They will be left for the beasts of the earth
They will be taken to another land
questions.correctAnswer: They will be left for the beasts of the earth
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:7 states that their carcasses will be given to be meat for the fowls of heaven and for the beasts of the earth as a consequence of their sins.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated by His willingness to bring evil upon the people?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:3 shows that God will bring evil upon the place due to the people's forsaking Him, demonstrating His justice in response to sin.

questions.question: What does God call the actions of the people towards other gods in Jeremiah 19:5?
questions.correctAnswer: An abomination
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 19:5, God expresses that the act of burning their sons as offerings to Baal is something He commanded not, indicating it as an abomination.

questions.question: How will the city become according to the prophecies in Jeremiah 19?
questions.correctAnswer: Desolate and an hissing
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:8 indicates that God will make the city desolate and an hissing, signifying a place of horror and desolation.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 19:9, what extreme behavior does God predict the people will resort to during the siege?
options: They will eat their own children
questions.correctAnswer: They will eat their own children
questions.explanation: The prophecy in Jeremiah 19:9 predicts that the people will resort to cannibalism, eating the flesh of their sons and daughters due to the dire circumstances.

questions.question: What does God say about the houses of Jerusalem in relation to Tophet?
questions.correctAnswer: They will be defiled
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:13 states that the houses of Jerusalem will be defiled like Tophet because of their idolatrous practices.

questions.question: What does God say about the counsel of Judah and Jerusalem in Jeremiah 19:7?
questions.correctAnswer: It will be made void
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 19:7, God declares that He will make void the counsel of Judah and Jerusalem due to their rebellion against Him.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah do after receiving the word from the Lord according to Jeremiah 19:14?
options: He prophesies in the court of the Lord's house
questions.correctAnswer: He prophesies in the court of the Lord's house
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:14 recounts that after coming from Tophet, he stood in the court of the Lord's house to proclaim the prophecy to the people.

questions.question: What overarching theme does Jeremiah 19 convey about the consequences of sin?
options: Sin leads to judgment and desolation
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to judgment and desolation
questions.explanation: The entire chapter of Jeremiah 19 illustrates that the people's persistent sin leads to severe judgment and desolation, as shown in multiple verses like 19:4 and 19:8.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the God of the Old Testament is solely a God of wrath. What does Jeremiah 19:15 actually teach about God's character?
options: God is just and holds people accountable
God does not care for His people
questions.correctAnswer: God is just and holds people accountable
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:15 reveals God's justice in bringing upon the city all the evil pronounced against it due to their hardening of hearts, showing that He holds people accountable for their actions.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 4-5 and verse 11 convey about the sin of the people?
options: Their sin leads to destruction and cannot be repaired
questions.correctAnswer: Their sin leads to destruction and cannot be repaired
questions.explanation: Verses 4-5 describe their abominable practices, while verse 11 illustrates that their destruction is irreversible, indicating the severe consequences of their sins.
